title: Percentage composition & purity
examples: How do I find the percentage composition of a mixture?
What is the difference between percentage composition and percent purity?
Can you show me an example of calculating percent purity?

explain.say: Today we will learn about percentage composition in mixtures. This tells us the parts by mass. We calculate this using the formula mass of component divided by total mass. Then we multiply by one hundred to get the percentage.

draw.text: % by Mass = (Mass of Component / Total Mass) × 100

explain.say: Let us look at a concrete example of percentage composition. Suppose you mix one gram of salt and three grams of sand. The total mass is four grams. The percentage of salt is twenty-five percent.

Next we will look at calculating the purity of a sample. Purity tells us how much of the desired substance is actually present. We use the same formula, but the component is the pure substance. The total mass is the sample mass.

draw.text: % Purity = (Mass of Pure Substance / Sample Mass) × 100

explain.say: Consider a sample of copper that weighs ten grams. We find it only contains nine point five grams of pure copper. The percentage purity is ninety-five percent.
In everyday life, you see percent purity in food labels. For example, a juice might say it is eighty percent apple juice. This means only twenty percent is added water or flavorings.
A common mistake is forgetting to divide by the total sample mass. Students sometimes divide by the mass of the pure substance instead. Always remember the total sample mass is the denominator.

draw.text: Total Mass is always the bottom number.

faq.q: What is the difference between percentage composition and percent purity?
faq.a: Percentage composition looks at the parts of a known mixture. Percent purity looks at how much of the pure substance is in the sample.
asks: How do I calculate percent purity?
Is composition the same as purity?
What does the denominator mean for purity?

faq.q: Do I need to know the molar masses for this calculation?
faq.a: No, for percentage by mass, you only need the measured masses of the components. Molar masses are used for mole calculations.
asks: Is this calculation based on moles?

faq.q: If I mix two things, do I add their percentages together?
faq.a: No, you must use the actual measured masses to find the true percentage composition. You cannot just add the percentages.
asks: Can I just add the percentages together?
What if the masses are different?

faq.q: What is 'sample mass' in percent purity?
faq.a: The sample mass is the total weight of the material you tested. This includes the pure substance and any impurities present.
asks: Is sample mass the total weight?
What is the denominator for purity?

faq.q: If I have a percentage, do I need to convert it to a decimal?
faq.a: Yes, if you use the percentage in a calculation later, you must divide it by one hundred to get the decimal form.
asks: Can I keep the percent sign?
How do I convert percent to decimal?

facts: Percentage composition shows the relative amounts of components in a mixture.
The formula for percent by mass is (mass of component / total mass) times one hundred.
Percent purity measures the fraction of a substance that is not contaminated.
The total mass in a mixture is found by adding the masses of all components.

quiz.say: A sample contains twenty grams of salt and three grams of sand. What is the percentage of salt?
quiz.why: The percentage is twenty divided by twenty-three, multiplied by one hundred.

wrong.0: This forgets to divide by the total mass.
wrong.2: This is the percentage of sand, which is the other component.
wrong.3: This incorrectly uses the salt mass as the total mass.

quiz.say: If a sample of metal weighs fifty grams and is only ninety percent pure, what is the mass of pure metal?
quiz.why: You calculate ninety percent of fifty grams to find the pure mass.

wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes the sample mass is one hundred grams.
wrong.2: This forgets to account for the impurity present in the sample.
wrong.3: This calculates the impurity mass instead of the pure mass.

quiz.say: A mixture has components A and B. Component A is 40% by mass, and Component B is 60% by mass. If the total mass is 100 grams, what is the mass of Component A?
quiz.why: Forty percent of one hundred grams is forty grams, which is the mass of Component A.

wrong.0: This incorrectly multiplies the percentage by one hundred.
wrong.1: This gives the mass of Component B instead of Component A.
wrong.2: This forgets to use the percentage to find the specific mass.
